name: Richard Nixon
role: Vietnamization: began pulling US troops out while shifting the fighting to the South Vietnamese army; widened the air war into Cambodia and Laos; signed the Paris Peace Accords; resigned twenty months before Saigon fell.

numbers.k: US troops at end of term
numbers.v: about 50 (Aug 1974); the last combat troops left 29 March 1973
~500,000 tons, 1969–1973, most of it after the ceasefire in Vietnam

numbers.k: Aid to Saigon voted for FY1975

decisions: Operation Menu: secret bombing of Cambodia begins, with falsified records.
Midway: first withdrawal of 25,000 announced; Vietnamization named by Laird.
Cambodian incursion announced; Kent State four days later.
Lam Son 719: ARVN into Laos without US ground troops; the test of Vietnamization, failed.
Beijing; then Moscow in May. The war becomes a detail in a larger deal.
Linebacker and the mining of Haiphong in answer to the Easter Offensive.
Kissinger: 'peace is at hand', twelve days before the election.
Linebacker II, the Christmas bombing, to bring Hanoi back and Thieu along.
Paris Peace Accords signed. Thieu given private letters promising a 'full force' response to violations; Congress never sees them.
Case–Church takes effect: no more US combat in Indochina.
Resigns. The promised response to violations goes with him.

advisers.post: National Security Adviser; Secretary of State from 1973
advisers.note: Ran the secret talks with Le Duc Tho from 1970; the 'decent interval'; the Nobel he accepted and Tho declined.
Kept out of the Vietnam channel by design.
Invented the word Vietnamization and pushed withdrawals faster than Kissinger wanted.
Schlesinger carried the aid fight into Ford's term.

advisers.post: Commander, MACV; Army Chief of Staff from 1972
advisers.note: Ran the withdrawal and the Cambodia incursion; built the ARVN that held in 1972 and broke in 1975.
Furled the MACV colours 29 March 1973; as Army Chief of Staff went back in April 1975 to report that Saigon could not hold without aid.
Linebacker and the mining; the Moorer–Radford affair, the JCS spying on the NSC.

advisers.post: Deputy National Security Adviser; Chief of Staff from 1973
advisers.note: Kissinger's deputy and Saigon courier; carried the pressure to Thieu in October 1972.
Refused to plan the evacuation until the last day; left on a helicopter from the embassy roof.
His son was a prisoner in Hanoi throughout.
Kept the diary; the domestic side of every decision.
The Plumbers were created after the Pentagon Papers.
The attack on the press and the 'nattering nabobs'.
Not in the four. Inherited the ending.

text: Nixon: out in four years, with the air war widened to two more countries, a treaty with private promises, and no one left to keep them.

articles: Obstruction of justice, the Watergate cover-up
Abuse of power: the IRS, the FBI, the CIA, the Plumbers
The secret bombing of Cambodia, 1969–1970, concealed from Congress
rejected 12–26 — the one Vietnam article, and the committee would not carry it
Taxes and the improvements at San Clemente and Key Biscayne
impeachment.note: The war he ran was put to the committee once, as Article IV, and voted down by both parties on the ground that Congress had known enough and funded it anyway. He resigned before the full House voted.

break.what: From the resignation to the Fall of Saigon: 264 days. The private letters to Thieu promising a “full force” response to violations were his; Congress had never seen them; Ford inherited a promise with no one to keep it. The break is the interval in which the guarantee behind Vietnamization turned out to be one man.
